header:
Date: 2026-01-15 
Start: 14:00 UTC 
Duration: 42 minutes 
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Brenner (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Peregrine Head of Search), Mark Wu (Peregrine SRE), Priya Nambiar (Peregrine ML), Devon Lee (Product)
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, and with me is Jules, our solutions engineer. Uh, quick agenda — we'll do a short intro, show the hosted embeddings endpoint, then a reranker pipeline demo and console tips.
[00:18] Lena: Great — thanks. We're mainly interested in improving our site search relevance and understanding costs.
[00:25] Jules: Awesome. Quick context question, Lena: what are you currently using for embeddings and ranking?
[00:32] Priya: We're on an in-house vectore store, FAISS, embeddings are generated with an open model, but quality varies; reranking is a simple BM25 + some logistic model.
[00:43] Mark: And infra-wise we run in GCP, VPC peering is possible but we have strict egress rules.
[00:51] Samir: Cool — that's helpful. We'll focus on hosted API so you can get value fast, but we'll call out dedicated and private for compliance.
[01:05] Jules: Alright, jumping into the demo — here on the console you can see the embeddings endpoint. The API is simple: POST /v1/embeddings with model param, returns a vector. Example payload and response in the docs.
[01:22] [01:22] (typing sounds)
[01:30] Jules: For reranking we provide a /v1/rerank endpoint. You send the query and a list of candidate passages (or IDs) and the service returns a score and an optional reordered list. Works well as a late-stage reranker after your initial recall.
[01:45] Lena: Do you support batch embeddings? We have millions of docs to index.
[01:50] Jules: Yes — batch endpoints and streaming supported. Also Redwood Optimize will recommend batch sizes based on your token/sequence distribution to minimize cost.
[02:05] Priya: How do you measure latency? Our SLAs are 200 ms p95 for interactive search.
[02:12] Samir: In hosted mode we publish p50/p95 profiles per model. Typical embedding call is 30–120 ms depending on model and vector dim. Rerank depends on number of candidates; reranking 10 candidates usually in 80–200 ms.
[02:28] Mark: If we need sub-100 ms consistently, sounds like dedicated pool?
[02:33] Jules: Dedicated capacity gives you predictable throughput and lower tail latency; we can model cost vs SLO. We also have autoscale+burst for spiky loads.
[02:45] Lena: Security — we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration.
[02:50] Samir: Yes, Redwood is SOC2-compliant; for Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM. Hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS in some regions; we'll share the compliance pack.
[03:05] Devon: Is there a way to keep raw text from leaving our VPC? I mean for hosted, that's a blocker for some teams.
[03:12] Jules: For strict data residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). Hosted keeps data encrypted in transit and at rest, and you can opt out of retention, but if you need zero egress we can discuss a dedicated or private deployment.
[03:27] Lena: Got it. Can you show an example rerank call with returned scores?
[03:33] Jules: Sure. I'll paste an example — query: "best noise cancelling headphones under $200" and five candidates. The reranker returns scores and an ordered list. In this case candidate 3 moves to top after rerank, improving MRR in our demo set.
[03:51] [03:51] (demo audio glitch for 2s)
[03:54] Priya: Sometimes the transcript shows "KV cash" instead of "KV cache" — small note.
[03:58] Jules: Yeah, transcription quirks. On the topic of caching, Redwood has prefix + KV cache to accelerate repeated contexts and reduce token compute.
[04:12] Mark: Do you have client libraries? We use Python and Go.
[04:16] Samir: Yes, Python/Go/TS SDKs, plus curl examples. SDKs handle batching and streaming. Jules can link the repo.
[04:24] Jules: Sharing the curl now in the chat: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-xxl","input":["text"]}' — response includes vector. For rerank: POST /v1/rerank with query+items.
[04:46] Lena: About cost — what's the per-embedding price and rerank price roughly for hosted?
[04:51] Samir: I'll send a detailed sheet, high level: embeddings priced per 1k vectors depending on model size; rerank billed per candidate evaluated and token compute. Optimize can reduce per-call cost by recommending smaller models for embeddings + caching.
[05:10] Priya: Can Optimize suggest quantization profiles?
[05:13] Jules: Yes — Optimize will suggest quantization and batching, and we can simulate quality loss vs cost in the console with your eval set. It surfaces recommended model variant and expected latency/cost impact.
[05:28] Devon: For A/B tests and rollouts, does the console support canary rerouting?
[05:32] Samir: Yes — per-route model pinning and canary rollouts, with tracing and per-token cost breakdowns visible.
[05:40] [05:40] (customer murmurs)
[05:48] Lena: Let's talk about evaluation. We need to ensure reranker doesn't introduce regressions on enterprise docs.
[05:54] Jules: We recommend a small offline eval harness — we'll provide a sample. Console can ingest eval results and trigger alerts for regressions. You can tie alerts to specific prompt sets.
[06:10] Mark: Networking — if we do hosted, can we restrict source IPs and use SAML for auth?
[06:15] Samir: Yes, IP allowlists, SAML/SSO, and RBAC available. For higher security, Private deployment is preferred.
[06:25] Priya: Are embeddings deterministic? We need stable vectors across re-index runs.
[06:29] Jules: Determinism depends on model and tokenizer. For smaller variance, use deterministic sampling-off models. We'll note that in the docs; Optimize can recommend stable model variants.
[06:45] Lena: Any gotchas for long documents?
[06:48] Jules: For long docs we recommend chunking + semantic chunk overlap; embeddings for chunks then rerank aggregated results. Redwood handles chunking tools in the console and suggests chunk size heuristics.
[07:05] Samir: I'm going to run a quick live example: query->recall->embeddings->rerank on a small product dataset.
[07:12] [07:12] (demo run)
[07:20] Jules: You can see the scoring delta — original recall returned item A, after rerank item B is more relevant and moves to top — measured CTR proxy improved in the demo set.
[07:40] Priya: Nice. How do we pass metadata like last_updated or product_category to the reranker?
[07:46] Jules: You include passthrough metadata or signal in the candidate payload; reranker can condition on those fields if you configure features. There's some manual feature wiring but the defaults work well.
[08:02] Lena: If we want to pilot, what minimal instrumentation do you need from our side?
[08:07] Samir: Ideally: a ~1k sample of queries with relevance judgments or click signals, access to a small index of candidate passages, and a test endpoint we can hit. We'll run a 2–4 week pilot.
[08:22] Devon: Will you sign an NDA?
[08:25] Samir: Yes — standard NDA, and we'll send the security/compliance pack after the call.
[08:32] Mark: For the pilot, can we simulate onprem data flow? We prefer not to send PII out.
[08:37] Jules: We can run a hybrid: keep raw data in your VPC and only exchange vectors or hashed IDs, or run Redwood Private trial in your GCP project for the pilot. We'll include options in the pilot proposal.
[08:55] Priya: About metrics — we use MRR and NDCG. Will you compute these in the console?
[08:59] Jules: Yes — console supports MRR/NDCG and custom metrics based on your label format. We can ingest your labels and show delta charts.
[09:12] Lena: Any limitation on candidate set size for rerank?
[09:16] Jules: Practically we suggest 5–50 candidates for efficient rerank. You can rerank larger lists but cost increases linearly; Optimize can recommend sweet spot for your workload.
[09:30] Samir: Okay, let's surface some engineering details — tokenization, sequence length, and kernel choices matter for latency.
[09:36] Jules: Right, our runtime picks optimized kernels automatically. For long sequences we can switch to quantized kernels which cut memory and cost but may slightly change outputs — Optimize will quantify that.
[09:50] [09:50] (brief silence)
[09:55] Devon: Curious about SLOs for hosted — do you guarantee p99?
[10:00] Samir: Hosted SLA covers availability; for tight latency SLOs we recommend Dedicated with SLA-backed latency targets. We'll model expected p95/p99 for the pilot.
[10:12] Priya: For the reranker model, can we bring our own checkpoint?
[10:16] Jules: You can bring models to Private or Dedicated in some plans; for hosted we serve curated model catalog. We can onboard custom models in partnership if needed.
[10:30] Lena: Ok, this is helpful. Anything else on observability?
[10:33] Samir: Console has per-route tracing, token-level cost, and error breakdowns. We also alert on quality regressions if you enable eval-based alerts.
[10:45] [10:45] (keyboard clacking)
[10:50] Jules: I'll paste the pilot checklist in chat now: dataset snippet, success metrics, target SLOs, contact list.
[11:00] Lena: Thanks. On pricing, do you offer committed discounts?
[11:03] Samir: Yes, committed reserved capacity and annual contracts for Dedicated. Hosted is usage-based but we can offer credits for pilots.
[11:15] Devon: Any partner integrators you recommend for complex onprem deploys?
[11:19] Samir: We have certified partners for onprem and MSPs; I'll include partner list in the follow-up.
[11:30] Priya: One last question — are embeddings versioned? If we reindex months later, can we map vectors across model versions?
[11:36] Jules: We version models and allow pinning. Mapping across versions is nontrivial; we recommend reindexing or using cross-encoders to align if needed.
[11:50] Samir: Great. To recap: we'll send pricing/pilot proposal and security pack; Jules will share benchmark harness and examples; Peregrine will provide a sample dataset and metrics.
[12:05] Lena: Sounds good. Let's target the kickoff on the 27th as discussed.
[12:12] Samir: Perfect — thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the docs.
[12:18] (call ends)
questions: Will hosted meet 200ms p95 for rerank at scale?
How to avoid sending raw PII to hosted?
Can Redwood run A/B experiments and compute MRR/NDCG in-console?
